ev.q: Of those responding to the individual questions, 33 of 42 (79%) stated they had difficulty obtaining INH within the last month
Difficulty obtaining INH in last month
At the time of the survey, six of 39 (15%) had run out of INH
79% of responding jurisdictions had experienced difficulty obtaining the first-line anti-tuberculosis drug, isoniazid (INH)
Number and percentage of jurisdictions reporting difficulty obtaining isoniazid (INH) during 2012–2013

public_health_question.v: What was the extent of the 2012–2013 isoniazid shortage and its impact on U.S. TB control programs?

ev.q: To assess the extent of the problem and its impact on TB control programs, a nationwide survey of programs was conducted
Impact of a Shortage of First-Line Antituberculosis Medication on Tuberculosis Control
surveyed 68 jurisdictions in 50 states, 10 large cities, five territories, and three freely associated island states, using a web-based questionnaire
a nationwide survey of programs was conducted in January 2013 by the National Tuberculosis Controllers Association (NTCA)
National Tuberculosis Controllers Association survey, United States

equity.level_reason: No social-position dimension; jurisdictions are described only by geography and TB case counts.

notes: Design inferred as cross-sectional from a one-time program survey. Program-level percentages are reported as single-group summaries with no comparisons or inference. The 6% rifampin figure comes from a separate informal webinar survey footnote.
view_issues: Response rate is 42/68 and denominators vary by question; the figure's state map values are not in the packet.
